data.narrative:
TAE Technologies is a Series G nuclear energy company that has raised $1.3B+ to date. The nuclear energy sector contains 10 comparable entities (3 public, 7 private), including peers such as Helion, Oklo, and X-Energy, though no exact stage or valuation-tier matches exist in sufficient quantity for robust peer-median analysis.

A stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using the $1.3B total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G advancement yields an implied valuation of $1.6B. This reflects the progression risk and dilution patterns observed in late-stage private financings. The peer-median method is not applicable due to insufficient narrow-set comparables—only one adjacent-stage peer exists within nuclear energy at similar scale, falling short of the three-datapoint minimum required for meaningful medianization.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B to $1.9B (median $1.6B), anchored to the stage-progression method. Key uncertainties include the absence of recent market transactions in this cohort, the technical and regulatory maturity of TAE's approach relative to peers, and the broad range of capital efficiency across the nuclear energy private market. Given reliance on a single method, confidence in this range is moderate; additional transaction or revenue-based data would strengthen conviction.
